title: Adaptive output surface for embedded clients (PRD sketch)
content:
Purpose: sketch a pragmatic, adaptive output surface that lets mobile/embedded clients and thin web SDKs consume streaming model output + tool calls with predictable resource usage and simple developer ergonomics. This is a working PRD sketch — lots of open questions below.

Context and motivation:
- Hosted API is pushing richer streaming semantics: typed frames, tool-call handshakes, partial structured output. Mobile and embedded clients struggle with memory, intermittent networks, and CPU for parsing/validation.
- We need a small-surface SDK contract that supports: progressive experience (first tokens quickly), structured tool calls (signals developers can act on), resume/replay for flaky networks, and graceful degradation to unstructured text.
- Goal: reduce customer integration work and edge-case bugs, while enabling lower-bandwidth clients to participate in the modern streaming tooling ecosystem.

High-level design principles:
1) Minimal client parsing: frames are small and labeled; client may ignore optional typed payloads.
2) Backward-compatible fallbacks: when client cannot parse structured frames, server provides plain-text fallback in the stream.
3) Checkpointed session snapshots: server emits small immutable session checkpoints that clients can request to resume state without replaying entire history.
4) Declarative tool signals: a compact tool-call envelope with explicit lifecycle events (invoke, progress, complete, error) to keep SDKs deterministic.
5) Network-first heuristics: SDK exposes policies to prefer lower-bandwidth frames (compact mode) and upgrade to rich frames when on WiFi.

User stories:
- Mobile app wants a snappy autocomplete UI that shows partial suggestions as they stream, but only needs tool call events when final result references an external action.
- A thin web widget must recover from intermittent connectivity: it should resume a conversation from a checkpoint without server re-evaluating earlier prompts.
- Platform integrator wants an SDK mode to validate structured outputs against a schema, but only on debug builds to avoid CPU overhead in production.

API surface (proposal) - simple, intentionally conservative:
- /v1/chat/stream (POST): headers: Accept-Frames: compact | rich | prefer-compact. Body: prompt + metadata + client-hint (network: wifi/cellular). Response: chunked stream of newline-delimited frames.
- Frame envelope (top-level): {"t":"<type>","id":"<frame-id>","ts":"<iso>","v":"<schema-v>"} + optional payload. (We will document formal JSON shapes separately.)
- Frame types (minimal set):
  - text.delta: incremental tokens (payload: utf8 chunk)
  - output.snapshot: lightweight checkpoint (payload: checkpoint-id, position, minimal metadata)
  - tool.invoke: declarative request to call a tool (payload: tool-id, args-ref or args-inline)
  - tool.progress: progress updates (payload: percent|stage)
  - tool.result: final tool output (payload: reference to structured result or small inline blob)
  - fallback.plain: guidance for clients that do not support structured frames, contains plain text with markers.
  - error: terminal errors with codes and optional remedial suggestions.

Client modes (SDK ergonomics) - four lightweight modes:
- compact: only text.delta and output.snapshot; tool frames collapsed to fallback.plain. Minimal parsing, for battery/CPU constrained clients.
- balanced: receive tool frames but do not validate schemas; pass tool payloads to integrator callbacks.
- strict-dev: validate structured payloads against schema-v on the client (for dev/debug).
- offline-first: keep short-lived checkpoints locally, attempt reconciliation on reconnect.

Session checkpoints and resume:
- Server emits output.snapshot frames periodically (configurable by model/route). Each snapshot includes: checkpoint-id, stable cursor into stream, light metadata (active tool calls, last-user-turn).
- Resume flow: client sends resume request with checkpoint-id and available local state. Server verifies and streams deltas from checkpoint cursor.
- Size targets: snapshot metadata under 2KB, default interval every 6-12s or after tool call completes.

Tool call lifecycle (ergonomics):
- Tool.invoke should be declarative and idempotent-friendly. Include a client-visible call-id so UI can render pending state.
- Prefer server-side execution with tool.result referencing an immutable artifact (url or id) instead of heavyweight inline JSON for mobile clients.
- Provide a client callback pattern in SDK: onToolInvoke, onToolProgress, onToolResult, onToolError. Callbacks receive the minimal frame envelope.

Structured output strategy and fallbacks:
- Schema versioning: frames have v field. SDKs can choose which versions to decode; unknown versions are surfaced as opaque payloads.
- Quiet-fallback: when structured parsing fails, SDKs map to fallback.plain frames and annotate telemetry to help us improve schema compatibility.

Telemetry and observability (what SDK should emit):
- events: frame_received(type), frame_parse_fail(reason), snapshot_saved(checkpoint-id), resume_attempt(result), onToolCallbackLatency(ms).
- send coarse telemetry only by default; opt-in for payload-level traces in debug builds.

Latency and bandwidth budget guidelines (defaults):
- compact mode: ~1KB/sec incremental target for token deltas on cellular.
- snapshot size <2KB.
- tool-progress updates coalesced to 1 per second max unless explicit stage changes.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Internal alpha: SDK + server-side frame plumbing on staging; product team and a couple of solutions-engineering customers.
2) Early access: invite mobile partners to test compact mode, collect telemetry.
3) Public beta: enable route flag for new streaming shape; provide fallback to existing streaming text-only route.
4) GA: enable by default for bandwidth-aware models and document migration guide.

Success metrics:
- Integration time: reduce time to integrate streaming+tools into a simple mobile app from 5 dev days to 2 dev days (survey).
- Resume success rate: >=95% resume without needing full context replay in early access tests.
- Client CPU impact: parsing overhead in compact mode should be <5% CPU on mid-tier phones in synthetic tests.
- Errors: frame_parse_fail rate <0.3% at GA.

Open questions and risks (note-to-self):
- How do we handle privacy-sensitive tool payloads in snapshots persisted on-device? Need KMS/HSM guidance for Private customers.
- Do we need signed snapshots to avoid tampering on resume? Tradeoff: complexity vs safety.
- Interactions with existing streaming SDKs: ensure minimal breakage for current customers that expect raw token streams.
- Rate of snapshots: snapshot frequency is a knob that interacts with server CPU and storage — need performance testing.
- Offline-first UX: how to surface conflicts if a client resumes with an older checkpoint? Conflict resolution policy required.

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Default server behavior: if client does not send Accept-Frames header, return legacy token-only chunks.
- API versioning: introduce route parameter and header to opt into adaptive surface. Avoid changing existing default route for 6+ weeks after beta.

Implementation tasks (engineering split):
- server: frame serializer, snapshot generator, compact-mode coalescing, tool lifecycle metadata persist.
- sdk: small parsers for compact envelope, lightweight checkpoint store, adapter callbacks, network heuristics to toggle modes.
- infra: storage for snapshots, observability pipeline for frame-level telemetry (sampling).

Dependencies and cross-team asks:
- Serving runtime: efficient snapshot creation without blocking token generation (ENG-serving-runtime).
- Console/observability: expose snapshots/resume traces in per-route timeline (product/console-and-rollouts).
- Security: guidance for snapshot encryption and retention for Private deployments (security-and-compliance).

Next steps (short-term):
- Run a quick spike to emit snapshot frames from a staging model for 72h and measure size/cpu. (Owner: Jonah)
- Draft the compact-mode SDK API and a minimal example mobile app integration (Owner: Priya)
- Collect 3 partner teams for early access (Owner: Marco)

Notes/links/brain dump:
- Prototype server shape: simple ndjson frames with leading metadata — easy for clients to parse with a tiny state machine.
- Consider adding an HTTP long-poll fallback for extremely flaky networks (no streaming transport).
- Playbook idea: provide a small reference mobile component that renders tool states and resumes from checkpoint, shipped as example in SDK repo.

Tags for internal search: adaptive-output, compact-streaming, snapshot-resume, tool-lifecycle, mobile-sdk.

---
This document is intentionally high-level and pragmatic. After initial spike we should produce a formal PRD with schema definitions, SDK methods, and end-to-end acceptance tests.
